results.finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts::the intentional commonmark deviation for a top-level `heading\n-` (single-dash setext h1... h2) is untested

verdict.reasoning: The `isLoneDash` guard in list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts (~lines 100-112) is unconditional on nesting, so a top-level `Heading\n-` — which markdown-it previously rendered as `<h2>` — now falls through to paragraph + empty list, a real user-visible deviation. The only setext test added, preview.test.ts:181-186, renders `Heading\n---` (runLength 3), which takes the guard's false branch and therefore never pins the lone-dash outcome; no other test in the full file exercises a `=` or single-`-` underline outside a list. The PR's own todo doc even lists "top-level lone dash" as an intended test case with the unit-test step left unchecked, corroborating the gap. This is a coverage gap for a deliberate deviation rather than a functional defect, hence minor.

results.finding_key: packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts::hand-rolled `asciitrim` uses a quadratic backtracking trim regex on attacker-controllable note content (redos → preview/tab hang)

verdict.reasoning: Verified at packages/notes/src/view/list-empty-bullet-plugin.ts:19-23: the global regex `/^[\x09...\x20]+|[\x09...\x20]+$/g` has an unanchored trailing alternative, so `String.replace` retries `[ws]+$` at every offset and backtracks the whole run each time — the textbook quadratic trim (trim-newlines / CVE-2021-33623 shape); `^` without `m` makes the first alternative cheap, so it offers no protection. It is applied to `state.getLines(...)` in the lheading heading branch (reached by any `Text\n===`/`---` paragraph), and preview.ts's `md.render` is synchronous and re-run from editor.ts's `docChanged` updateListener, so a note containing a long internal whitespace run followed by non-whitespace freezes the tab on every edit or remote patch. I could not execute the code or inspect the installed markdown-it to confirm the secondary claim that upstream `lheading` uses native `.trim()`, but the quadratic pattern exists in this file as written. Severity is major rather than critical: it is a crafted-input, availability-only DoS requiring a very large whitespace run from a collaborator, not a data or integrity compromise.
